Name: Stardew Item Studio
Author: Jrollsons
Description:
[b]Description[/b]
Stardew Item Studio is a free Windows app that lets you create your own Stardew Valley furniture mods, no coding, no config files, no modding experience needed. If you can draw pixels, you can make a mod.

I made this because I'm a total noob at modding myself,  even the "beginner-friendly" guides felt like a barrier, with JSON files, sprite index maths and rotation layouts to get right before you ever see your furniture in-game. I wanted something where you just draw your item and press export. 

You draw your furniture on canvases that are exactly the sizes the game uses (including the extra angles for rotatable furniture like chairs and couches), and the app turns your artwork into a complete, working Content Patcher mod,  ready to drop into your Mods folder, or upload right here to Nexus as your own furniture pack.

⚠️ This is an early concept version! It works end-to-end, but I'm releasing it early because I want feedback from the community. If you make something with it, hit a problem, or wish it did something it doesn't,  please tell me in the posts tab. Every comment helps shape the next version.

[b]Installation instructions[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Download the file and unzip it anywhere (your Desktop is fine).[/*]
[*]Double-click StardewItemStudio.exe, that's it, there's nothing to install.[/*]
[*]Windows may show a "Windows protected your PC" warning the first time (the app isn't code-signed, normal for free hobby tools). Click "More info" → "Run anyway".[/*]
[/list]Note: the app itself does NOT go in your Stardew Valley Mods folder, it's a standalone editor. Only the furniture packs you export with it go into Mods.
[b]Main features[/b]
[list]
[*]🪑 17 furniture types, chairs, couches, benches, tables, rugs, lamps, fireplaces, paintings, bookcases and more, each with the correct in-game canvas size and footprint[/*]
[*]🔄 Rotation frames done for you, rotatable furniture gets labeled Front / Right / Back sections laid out exactly the way the game reads them (the fiddliest part of furniture modding, handled automatically)[/*]
[*]🎨 Full pixel editor, pencil, eraser, fill, line, rectangle, eyedropper (right-click to pick a color), mirror mode, undo/redo, zoom, pixel + tile grids[/*]
[*]🌈 Big color selection, curated Stardew-style palettes plus classic pixel-art palettes (Endesga 64, Resurrect 64, AAP-64 and more), a free color picker and recent-colors history[/*]
[*]🖼️ Whole pack on one screen, every item in your furniture set side by side, all editable, so your style stays consistent[/*]
[*]💾 Project files,  save your work and come back to it any time[/*]
[*]📦 One-click export, produces a finished Content Patcher mod folder for testing AND a Nexus-ready zip; your furniture shows up in the in-game Furniture Catalogue (and optionally Robin's shop)[/*]
[*]❓ Built-in beginner's guide covering drawing tips, testing your mod, and uploading to Nexus[/*]
[/list][b]Requirements[/b]
To use the editor itself: nothing, just Windows 10 or 11.
To play the furniture packs you create (or share), the standard Stardew modding setup is needed:
[list]
[*]SMAPI — the mod loader (smapi.io)[/*]
[*]Content Patcher — by Pathoschild (Nexus mod #1915)[/*]
[/list]Both are one-time installs and the in-app guide walks you through them.
[line]
Known limitations of this concept version (so you can paste them too if you like): beds and fish tanks aren't supported yet, there's no PNG import or recolor tool yet, and exported packs target Stardew Valley 1.6+. Feedback on which of these matters most to you is exactly what I'm looking for!
